newsitem.title: NORWAY: Statoil upgrades Statfjord North reserve.
newsitem.headline: Statoil upgrades Statfjord North reserve.

text.p: Official estimates for recoverable oil reserves from its Statfjord North oilfield have been upgraded by about 55 million barrels to 230 million, Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil ) said on Thursday.
This means the recovery factor for the North Sea field and nearby Statfjord East has risen to 60 per cent, assuming production continues until the year 2020, Statoil's Status Weekly newsletter said.
"The upgrading reflects new information about and enhanced understanding of the reservoir," Tore Henrik Guldbrandsoey, head of resource utilisation for the Statfjord satellites, said.

"We've recently completed the four-year primary drilling programme on these two fields," he said. "Embracing 18 wells, this has given us additional geological and reservoir data. We've confirmed that Statfjord North extends rather further than first thought."
An upgrading of water-injection capacity on the satellites, planned for next year, is also expected to help recover more of the oil in place, Status Weekly said.
It said plans called for one additional producer and another water-injection well to be drilled on Statfjord North in 1998 to optimise drainage of the field.

Production from the satellites began in 1994, and they currently flow about 160,000 barrels per day from 13 production wells. The two are produced through subsea installations tied back to Statfjord C.
